requestedActions.title: Read issue titles in a project the connected person can access, with pagination
Authorize the app to access the connected person's GitLab account via OAuth

guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth app registration, user authorization, and token use for third-party access. The issue list endpoint is documented with keyset pagination. The issue-read scope identifier is not in the supplied sources, so the read permission is unresolved. Register an OAuth app and test authorization first. Then test the GET issue list with the OAuth Bearer header. Customer distribution review requirements are unknown, so they stay a launch-stage check.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read issue titles in a project the connected person can access, with pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: OAuth requests use the Bearer header, not the personal token header
findings.detail: Use the documented OAuth Authorization Bearer header for API calls. Do not copy the PRIVATE-TOKEN header from the issue examples.

--header "Authorization: Bearer <OAUTH-TOKEN>" \

findings.title: Connected person's project role governs visibility
findings.detail: Roles define what a user can access in a project. A minimal-access role grants none of the project permissions, so the test user needs project access.

evidence.quote: Roles define a user’s permissions in a group or project.
The Minimal Access role grants none of the permissions in the group and project permission tables.

steps.title: Test reading issue titles in a project
steps.detail: Call the issue list for one project the test account can access, using the OAuth Bearer header. Replace the instance host and project ID placeholders. Expected response: a JSON array with issue titles. Boundary check: Confirm the request was GET only, the outgoing log shows no POST, PUT, or DELETE calls, and the granted scope list is the one selected.
steps.doneWhen: The response is a JSON array of issues with titles, and the request log shows only GET.

steps.title: Test paginating through project issue titles
steps.detail: Request a follow-up page using the cursor from the first response. The method is still GET only. Expected response: a different page of issue titles. Boundary check: Confirm only GET calls appear in the log and no issue data was changed.
steps.doneWhen: A second page with different issue titles is returned using the cursor.
